newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi said to be "determined" to put Italy in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Prodi said to be "determined" to put Italy in EMU.

text.p: Italian prime minister Romano Prodi is determined to get Italy into Europe's single currency, the leader of a centrist party in Italy's ruling coalition said.

Franco Marini, leader of the centrist Popular Party (PPI), met Prodi earlier on Thursday and said afterwards they had discussed the issue of Italy's entry into European economic and monetary union (EMU), due to start in 1999.
"The prime minister seems very determined to me," Marini said.

Italian financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore has reported in the last two days that a deal was taking shape between Germany and France to delay Italian EMU entry and keep Spain out of the first wave as well.
Italy, France and Germany have all denied that a secret deal exists on EMU entry.
